text:
maria: Heads-up — saw steady GPU memory growth on gpu0 during the long-ctx perf harness (10k tokens). Profiler points at repeated KV handoff loops + continuous-batching merge churn. snapshot attached to the run (not pasted).

alex: Can you paste the hottest stacks / a short log excerpt? Is this only long contexts or also mid-length? :eyes:

maria: quick log snippet from the run:
```
2024-06-18T09:12:02Z gpu0 KV_RESERVE slot=42 ctx=client-ff tail=180s wait=120ms
2024-06-18T09:12:02Z gpu0 CONTBATCH merge_attempt=1 -> wait_for_handoff
2024-06-18T09:12:02Z gpu0 KV_RESERVE slot=43 ctx=client-gg tail=181s wait=118ms
2024-06-18T09:12:02Z gpu0 CONTBATCH merge_attempt=2 -> backoff(0ms)
2024-06-18T09:12:03Z gpu0 CONTBATCH merge_attempt=3 -> backoff(0ms)
2024-06-18T09:12:03Z gpu0 KV_FREE slot=42 ctx=client-ff
2024-06-18T09:12:04Z gpu0 KV_RESERVE slot=42 ctx=client-hh wait=200ms
```
Notable: merge_attempts climb quickly with effectively zero backoff in the hot path.

jamal: Flame graph shows two recurring hotspots: kv_reserve_slot (blocking) and contbatch_wait_merge. It looks like a livelock/handshake: batch A holds a slot reservation waiting for B to finish merging, B waits for A's prefix to free, repeat. Head-of-line blocking cascades because the merge window never closes.

samantha: I repro'd locally with the stress-harness. Steps: run harness --long-ctx --contbatch=true --kv-frag=high --burst=200, after ~5m mem climbs and throughput drops. I captured perf samples — attaching gist (omitted here).

maria: Mitigation experiments I tried: 1) add a randomized exponential backoff before a merge handoff (base 2ms), 2) cap contbatch merge_attempts to 8 per-slot, 3) fallback to non-merge execution path when kv_fragmentation > 0.6.

alex: Results?

maria: Canary numbers (30m window):
- baseline tail growth: +42% mem over 30m
- with backoff+cap: +9% mem over 30m
- p99 latency: +4ms (small), throughput same-ish
So big win on memory growth, small latency cost.

ci-bot: build/contbatch-handoff-backoff passed (linux/gpu) :white_check_mark:

jamal: Nice. Also propose kernel-selection hint: when merge_attempts > 4 prefer narrow-kernel (lower peak memory) to avoid long-kernel preemption of other batches — that lets us keep latency while easing pressure on KV slots.

alex: Good call. We saw cases where large attention kernels hold memory for 100s ms while contbatch keeps queuing. If we bias toward small-kernel early, we may break the handshake.

maria: I'll add the kernel hint to the PR and run another canary. Patch will: add randomized backoff, merge_attempt cap=8, kernel_hint_on_merge_failures=prefer-narrow. PR link: https://git.redwood/pr/3982 (will post when created)

samantha: Re-run checklist: long-ctx perf harness, canary on dedicated pool, run for 2h with metrics on kv_reservations, contbatch_merge_attempts, mem_growth. I can take the canary run tomorrow. :+1:

alex: If canary looks good, rollout to dedicated and notify SRE to watch for latency regressions (p95/p99). Also add regression test to stress-harness that fails if mem growth > 20% over 1h.

maria: Opening PR now. Thanks team.

jamal: TL;DR: contbatch merge handshake -> livelock -> kv slot hoarding -> long-ctx mem growth. Short-term: backoff + cap + kernel hint. Medium: consider merge window redesign (epochs) or explicit handoff token with timeout.

ci-bot: canary deploy queued to cluster:dedicated-canary-3 at 1749995600

alex: ping @sre for post-deploy watch.

samantha: noted. I'll collect traces and flamegraphs during canary window.

maria: thanks — will update thread with PR and canary results. :thumbsup:
